chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Hot food was brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not Feed us the fire. Set it aside until it cools.' So it was left until it cooled.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling or etiquette regarding eating hot food?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) practical wisdom in avoiding 'fire' (excessive heat) to preserve bodily health, a concept later expanded by Shia jurists into the etiquette of eating. It underscores the principle of moderation in consumption, linking physical well-being to spiritual discipline by preventing the haste and discomfort associated with hot food.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘They came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> with hot food, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic does not Feed us the fire. Keep it aside until it cools’. So it was left until it cooled’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘Once, hot food was brought to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, is not the one to feed us what is similar to fire. Wait, until it becomes cold’, thus, it was left to become cold.’”
